sources.entry: matplotlib - A comprehensive library for creating static, animated, and interactive visualizations.

summary.one_liner: Matplotlib is a Python library for creating static, animated, and interactive data visualizations and publication-quality figures.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Matplotlib as a comprehensive plotting library for static, animated, and interactive visualizations in Python. It says the library produces publication-quality figures in a variety of hardcopy formats and interactive environments across platforms. It states it can be used in Python scripts, Python/IPython shells, web application servers, and various GUI toolkits. The README itself is brief and mostly links out to the home page, install docs, contributing guide, and discussion channels for detail. It also asks users who publish work made with Matplotlib to cite it, and links to a ready-made citation entry.
use_cases: make static plots in Python scripts
embed interactive plots in GUI applications
generate plots for web application servers
how_to_run: See the install documentation (generated from /doc/install/index.rst) for installation instructions
